clue.text: Extensively think about, and do, guide to cutting exciting love with small, square Anne

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them, to con them
a template is a pattern that guides a cutter's blade or scissors

indicators.note: exciting stirs things up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A rambling instruction about thinking, cutting and an excited Anne, with a squared-off love affair thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exciting' stirs LOVE, S and ANNE into ONES NAVEL; 'square' has no clear job, and even the puzzle's blog commenters could not account for it. 'do' is the swindling sense, as in 'I've been done'.
explanation.definitionFit: Navel-gazing is idle, prolonged introspection, so the phrase means to mull something over at great length without acting.

clue.text: Source of games I play deviously with Mo

indicators.note: acting deviously means not going straight, so the letters wander into another order

explanation.surface: Someone plays a crafty game against a person called Mo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deviously' rearranges I PLAY plus MO. Olympia in Greece was the site of the ancient Olympic Games.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia, in the Peloponnese, was the sanctuary where the ancient Olympic contests were first held.

clue.text: Sign of times, collecting three points in league?

indicators.note: collecting means taking something in, so one piece gathers the other inside it

parts.note: T stands for time, so times is the plural TS
in league football a victory earns three points, so it is a win

explanation.surface: A question about a team picking up a victory in its league, as a sign of the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' is a sign of the zodiac, Gemini; 'collecting' is the container signal. Using T for time and so TS for times is unusual, and some solvers objected to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the third sign of the zodiac, is pictured as a pair of brothers born together.

clue.text: Harlem's decomposing composer

indicators.note: decomposing means breaking down, so the letters of the place name fall apart and re-form

parts.note: the New York district's name, taken as written without the possessive

explanation.surface: Something from Harlem is rotting away, and it belongs to a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decomposing' rearranges HARLEM; the word neatly echoes 'composer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Mahler was the Austrian late-Romantic who wrote nine completed symphonies.

clue.text: "Flexible lecturer" describes your compiler to a T!

parts.note: is serves as describes, as in 'that is me'
to a T means exactly, which here is so, as in 'just so'
the setter refers to themself, so the compiler is me

explanation.surface: The setter says the phrase "Flexible lecturer" describes them perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'L is so me': L plus IS SO ME. 'Your compiler' is the setter, so ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome describes a body that is supple, lithe and moves easily.

clue.text: Ready to accept flash spread about romantic couples?

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole assembly is read backwards
to accept means taking something in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: ready as an adjective means prepared or set
a flash is a moment, a mo
to sow seed is to spread it

explanation.surface: Is someone poised to take on flashy spreads about lovers?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' builds SEMOSOWT and 'about' then turns the whole of it round, not just one piece. 'flash' means an instant, as in 'in a flash'.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a pair of people, here the dating kind.

clue.text: Striking and more appropriate clothier, say

parts.note: workers on strike are out
something more appropriate is fitter

explanation.surface: Someone striking and more suitable as a clothes seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like an adjective meaning impressive; it is workers who are on strike, OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter sells clothing, and a clothier is one example of that trade.

clue.text: Arise from Greek character with title in revolution

indicators.note: in revolution means turning right round, so the whole pairing is read backwards

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a title is a name

explanation.surface: Something emerges from a Greek with a title during a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' turns ETA + NAME into EMAN + ATE. 'Greek character' suggests a person; it is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate from something is to issue or come out of it.

clue.text: How, twice on the air, an original was sustained legally

indicators.note: on the air means broadcast, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: the first sustained powered flight was made by the Wright brothers

explanation.surface: Something about a lawful first achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How an original was sustained' is 'by Wrights', the brothers who made the first sustained flight, and 'on the air' both puns on flight and signals the sound. 'twice' points to the two brothers; even the puzzle's blog found this loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by rights means doing it properly, according to what is lawfully due.

clue.text: With University entry, The InComplete Angler backs ban

indicators.note: with university entry means the U goes into the other letters
backs means goes backwards, so the shortened name is read in reverse
incomplete means one letter short, so the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Izaak Walton wrote The Compleat Angler

explanation.surface: A ban on a fishing book once a university gets involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'InComplete' puns on Izaak Walton's book The Compleat Angler: WALTON loses its last letter, 'backs' reverses WALTO to OTLAW, and 'entry' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlaw something is to prohibit it.

clue.text: Gloomiest place I vandalised — with knowledge

indicators.note: something vandalised is smashed up, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone wrecked the most depressing spot, fully aware of what they were doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalised' rearranges GLOOMIEST PLACE I.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistemology is the philosophy of knowledge, so the adjective means concerned with knowledge.

clue.text: See 1
Wanting to mess about? Text "Erica" free

indicators.note: wanting to mess about means eager to fool around with things, so the letters get shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone wants to fool around, so a text frees a woman called Erica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting to mess about' rearranges TEXT ERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate someone is to release them from a difficulty.

clue.text: Part of Olympics, say, watched outside (just in the minority?)

indicators.note: outside means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: something watched has been seen
the Olympics are made up of events

explanation.surface: Part of the Olympics is watched outside, by only a small group.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: at seventeen you are just still a minor, one year short of the age of majority, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aged seventeen is a minor for one last year before reaching adulthood at eighteen.

clue.text: Where romantically to settle heart?

parts.note: the heart is the traditional emblem of love
to settle someone is to seat them

explanation.surface: A question about where to settle one's heart in a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settle' looks like a verb but also matches SEAT, and a loveseat is a small sofa for two, where a couple sits romantically.
explanation.definitionFit: A loveseat is a small two-person sofa, a cosy place for a courting couple.

clue.text: Target of river directors

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon, in south-west England
a company's directors make up its board

explanation.surface: The aim of some riverside company directors.
explanation.walkthrough: The DART is a river in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A dartboard is the circular target that darts are thrown at.

clue.text: Start off chaos with a party? It's pear-shaped

indicators.note: start off means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: havoc is chaos
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Things go wrong when chaos starts at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' removes H from HAVOC. 'pear-shaped' suggests things going wrong; it is literal, since the avocado is pear-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is a tropical fruit roughly the shape of a pear, also called the alligator pear.

clue.text: Like figure 666 glimpsed in unorthodox choir

indicators.note: glimpsed in means seen within, so one piece sits inside the other
unorthodox means not following the usual form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: 666 is the Mark of the Beast in Revelation, abbreviated MB

explanation.surface: The number of the beast is spotted in a strange choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' gives CIHOR, a jumble of the choir's letters, and 'glimpsed in' sets the beast's mark within it. 666 is the number of the Beast in Revelation, and its Mark is M B.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a geometric figure, so rhombic means shaped like that figure.

clue.text: Total value left by couple in Row 144?

parts.note: a gross is twelve dozen, 144
a domestic is a household quarrel, especially in police slang
a couple's child is their product, what they leave behind

explanation.surface: An estate total left by a couple who lived in house number 144 on a street called Row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is a quarrel, not a street: a domestic. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A country's GDP is the total value of goods and services it produces in a year.

clue.text: Breaking pencil's producing anger for Shakespeare

indicators.note: breaking means smashing apart, so the letters re-form

explanation.surface: Breaking a pencil makes Shakespeare angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' rearranges PENCILS, possessive s included. The spleen was held to be the seat of anger, a sense common in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: The spleen was thought the source of ill temper, so in Elizabethan use its adjective meant irascible.

clue.text: Two trees next to which to remove church stone

parts.note: the ash is a tree

indicators.note: to remove means the named letters are taken out

parts.note: the larch is a tree

explanation.surface: Beside two trees a church is to be cleared away, leaving stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remove' takes CH from LARCH, leaving LAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is dressed, squared building stone laid in regular courses.

clue.text: Bobby studies set of figures following work over unwanted invaders

indicators.note: following means these pieces come after the ones that follow in the clue
over means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
lice are unwelcome creatures that infest hair
to con is to study
a table is a set of figures

explanation.surface: A policeman studies statistics after work on getting rid of pests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bobby' is British slang for a policeman, after Sir Robert Peel, who founded the Metropolitan Police. 'over' turns the work round, and 'following' places the studies and figures after the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobby is the British nickname for a uniformed police officer.

clue.text: Help, when credit's limited, sharpish

indicators.note: limited means confined, so one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: aid is help
CR is the standard abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Help is needed quickly when credit is restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharpish' suggests quickly; here it means sharp-tasting or pungent. 'limited' is the container signal: the help confines the credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means pungent or biting, sharp to taste or smell.

clue.text: Is possible to provide imitation sofa

parts.note: can means is able, is possible
to ape is to imitate

explanation.surface: Is it possible to supply a fake sofa?
explanation.walkthrough: A canape here is the French word for a sofa, also used in English, not the snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Canapé in French furniture means a settee or couch.

clue.text: Male circle's place of engagement

parts.note: a bull is a male animal
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A male's ring, as at an engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' suggests a betrothal ring; it is the fight between matador and bull.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullring is the arena where bullfights take place.
